key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning outperformed the multitask neural network in predicting UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, with the largest gains for UTS.
engineering_relevance: Accurate weld-property predictions could support process optimization and structural-integrity assessment.
method: Compare a shared-layer multitask neural network with stacking ensemble learning.
Predict UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected-zone (HAZ) hardness using a shared dataset.
Evaluate each target using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved R² values of 0.9863, 0.9782, and 0.8453 for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, respectively, versus 0.6724, 0.9215, and 0.8407 for the multitask network.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE scaling, limiting assessment of generalizability and physical prediction error.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
